TrustedSigner.description: TrustedSigner is one signer and what it may sign. Its identity fields mean what they mean in Signer.

identity.description: Identity is the keyless certificate identity, exactly (a GitHub Actions workflow: https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/.github/workflows/ FILE@REF); IdentityRegexp matches it instead, anchored with ^ and naming the owner exactly (ending it with /), never a wildcard.

issuer.description: Issuer is the OIDC issuer of the certificate, e.g. https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com.

key.description: Key is a public key (a file relative to this document, or a KMS URI) instead of a certificate identity.

name.description: Name labels the signer in reports and messages.

roles.description: Roles is what the signer may sign: image (an image's signature and attestations; the default), stack (a clearcutt-factory stack), and/or estate (an estate report bundle or history index in a registry, as clearcutt-verify estate pull and estate history read them).

sourceMatchesImage.description: SourceMatchesImage requires the signing run to be in the repository the image names as its source (org.opencontainers.image.source).

sourceRef.description: SourceRef is the ref the signing run must be on, e.g. refs/heads/main.

sourceRepository.description: SourceRepository is the one repository (https://github.com/OWNER/REPO) whose workflow runs may sign: the certificate's Source Repository URI must be it. For a reusable workflow, the calling repository.

sourceRepositoryOwner.description: SourceRepositoryOwner accepts runs in any repository of one owner (https://github.com/OWNER): the certificate's Source Repository URI must be https://github.com/OWNER/<repo>, i.e. its owner segment must be OWNER, and that repository is then required of cosign exactly (--certificate-github-workflow-repository). An alternative to SourceRepository for a reusable workflow every repository of an organization calls; with SourceRepository or SourceMatchesImage too, the repository they resolve to must be the owner's.

tlog.description: Tlog false accepts this key signer's evidence without a transparency log entry (cosign --insecure-ignore-tlog), for a key that signs without one. Keyless signers can't set it.

description: TrustPolicy says whose signatures an organization accepts, and for what. The ClearCutt tools share it: clearcutt-verify checks an estate's evidence against its image signers, and clearcutt-factory (signing.trustPolicy) checks images and stacks against it when building, publishing, and rebasing.

signers.description: Signers are the trusted signers; evidence verifies if any applicable one vouches for it.

title: ClearCutt trust policy
